notes: Latest source: Water Safety Ireland, National Drowning Report 2023/2024 With Rolling Report 2018 to 2022 (published Nov 2025, CSO Tables VSA35 and VSA29 extracted 01/05/2025). No newer edition was found; WSI's statistics page (modified 2026-10-12) links it as the latest and adds 2025 (80, provisional). Status partial: Ireland prints no setting split for its latest year. The report's split ("In Focus: Bodies of Water", pp.32-34) is pooled 2018-2022 and only three categories are printed in text (dock areas 54, canals 51, rivers 151) beside the two groups (made 141, natural 439); the remaining categories (pools, quarries, drains, slurry pits, tanks/wells, bath tubs; lakes, beaches, sea rocks, open sea, bogs) sit in Figures 19 and 22, whose labels extract scrambled. The one single-year setting figure in prose (natural waters: 110 in 2018, 71 in 2022) is recorded. The statistics page adds a 2019-2023 pooled split of accidental drownings (natural water 128, boating 11, domestic/pool 5, unspecified 250 of 394) in which 63.5% have no location. Definition: the report gives no formal definition of drowning; the Foreword says WSI "defines drownings as preventable injuries and tragedies". The counts are CSO cause-of-death records ("Every drowning incident recorded by the CSO attracts an ICD classification code", p.28) in three classes: accidental, deaths by suicide, and unclassified (undetermined, assault, other). So the totals and the setting rows are ALL INTENTS; suicides are 35.8% of 2018-2022 and are concentrated in docks, canals, rivers, beaches and lakes (rows ireland-suicide-location-*). Water transport is INCLUDED: Boating is an action category (7 of 578; the seven action categories on p.28 add up to 578) and the statistics page counts "boating incidents" (11 of 394 accidental, 2019-2023). The CSO has assigned "almost all unclassified drownings to an appropriate ICD-10 code" (p.15). Provisional CSO data have historically run about 10% below final (p.13). Overseas deaths of Irish nationals are listed separately. Disagreements the reviewer should look at by eye: (1) 2023 total is 78 in the report (provisional, 01/05/2025) but 129 on the statistics page (Oct 2026), a 65% revision, both recorded as separate rows; (2) the statistics page's 2019-2023 Quick Facts (607, 394 accidental) do not reconcile with its own yearly rows for those years (125, 106, 102, 100, 129; accidental 70, 68, 57, 73, 95) and the page prints 2019 as 125 in one table and 126 in another; (3) the report's made (141) and natural (439) groups add up to 580, not 578, while the rivers share (26.1%) is computed on 578; (4) the 2025 block names Coast Guard, Garda, coroner and media sources under a "Provisional data from the Central Statistics Office" label. Chart reading, NOT recorded as rows, for a person to verify in the PDF: the by-classification charts (Figures 20 and 21) carry labels that, matched against the statistics page's yearly intent totals, read as made waters 35, 27, 22, 28, 29 and natural waters 110, 98, 84, 74, 71 for 2018-2022 (natural: accidental 63, 52, 50, 46, 53; suicide 38, 45, 32, 27, 18); Figure 19 (canal, dock area, other made by year) cannot be assigned to years with confidence. The checker prints twelve numeric-coincidence warnings (58 = 54 + 4, 58 = 7 + 51, 64 = 7 + 57, 71 = 7 + 64, 78 = 7 + 71, 128 = 71 + 57, 129 = 51 + 78, 129 = 71 + 58, 151 = 71 + 80, 11 = 7 + 4): accidents of small integers; every row is a figure as printed and nothing was added across rows. Pooled rows carry year = end of period, as the canada-location-* rows do. Grade A is used for the statistics page because it is WSI's own publication of CSO data; the reviewer may prefer C for the 2025 collation. Not comparable with australia-location-2024-25, uk-waid-2024, canada-location-* or new-zealand-location-* without harmonising intent and taxonomy. No name, contact detail or precise position was recorded.
